points.description: States that insertion and deletion operations can be performed in constant time (O(1)) in a doubly-linked list (equivalent wording accepted, e.g. efficient/fast without traversal).

States that this holds including for operations before a given location or at the end of the list (e.g. via the previous pointer / tail access, without traversing from the head, unlike a singly-linked list).

rubric.notes: Full marks: constant-time insertion/deletion and that this includes operations before a given node or at the end. Half: only one of the two ideas. No marks: unrelated advantages only (e.g. just 'can traverse backwards' with no mention of efficiency).
